title: 稳压器的压差：电池越来越没电时
summary: ESP32 拔掉 USB，只靠 LM1117-3.3 稳压器供电。把输入电压往下调，像一节慢慢没电的锂电池：3.3 V 什么时候守不住，芯片什么时候复位？
concepts: 线性稳压器 linear regulator / LDO
description: 稳压电源 → LM1117-3.3（输入、输出各 10 µF）→ ESP32 的 3V3 脚，ESP32 不插 USB；一个输出高的 GPIO 串 330 Ω 点亮红色 LED，表示芯片在运行。线性稳压器只能降压，输入至少要比输出高一个压差（这里约 1.1 V）；多出来的电压全部变成热。

cards.title: 把电池慢慢“用完”
text: 这次 ESP32 **不插 USB**：单击它，在右侧「属性」里取消勾选**「USB 供电」**。它只能靠你给的电。
**稳压电源**（`5 V`）的 + 接 **LM1117-3.3** 的 IN（正面朝你，三只脚是 GND、OUT、IN），稳压器的 OUT 接 ESP32 的 **3V3** 脚，GND 都连在一起。
任意一个 GPIO 设成**「输出 高」**，串 **`330 Ω`** 接一颗**红色 LED** 到 GND。LED 亮着，就说明芯片在运行。
现在把稳压电源从 `5 V` **一点一点往下调**，像一节越用越没电的锂电池。LED 在哪里熄灭？输入明明还有 3 V 多，为什么不够？

cards.title: 稳压器是一个自动拧的水龙头
text: - 线性稳压器像串在输入和输出之间的一个**自动拧的水龙头**。输入多出来的电压它都吃掉，输出就稳在 3.3 V。
- 可是水龙头全开时，自己也要吃掉一段电压，叫**压差**。输入再往下降，输出只能跟着降。本仿真里 LM1117 的压差是 1.1 V 再加 0.2 Ω：
- 代入数字：输入 3.6 V、电流 0.05 A 时，$V_{OUT} = 3.6 - 1.1 - 0.2 × 0.05 = 2.49$ V。已经掉到 ESP32 的欠压线以下，芯片复位，所有引脚松开，LED 灭。
![](fig:dropout)
- 反过来，输入很高时输出照样是 3.3 V，但多出来的电压 × 电流，全部变成稳压器上的**热**。

cards.title: 加上电容，再测一遍
text: - 两个 **`10 µF`**：一个从 IN 到 GND，一个从 OUT 到 GND，都插在稳压器旁边。真实的 LM1117 没有输出电容可能自己振荡。
- 电源调回 **`5 V`**，点**「检查我的电路」**。检查会把电源依次调到 5 V、4.0 V、3.7 V、3.4 V 和 9 V，看输出和 LED。
- 通过后，按测量题把电源调到对应的电压，用万用表和电流表读数。先预测：4.0 V 在水龙头全开的那一段吗？
- 9 V 那几道题算的是稳压器的发热：它两端的电压乘以流过它的电流。

cards.title: 带走
text: - **线性稳压器只能降压**，输入至少要比输出高一个压差（LM1117 约 1.1 V）。低于这一点，输出跟着输入往下掉。
- 多出来的电压全变成热：$P = (V_{IN} - V_{OUT}) × I$。12 V 降到 3.3 V 时，大部分电能都烧在稳压器上，这时该用开关电源。
- 真实项目里的坑：**一节锂电池（3.0–4.2 V）+ AMS1117-3.3** 是经典错误。电池一降到 4 V 左右，3.3 V 就守不住，ESP32 一开 Wi-Fi 就重启。要选压差只有 0.1–0.25 V 的**低压差稳压器**（如 ME6211、HT7333）。
- 外部电源接 3V3 脚时，**不要同时插 USB**：两个电源会互相打架。

caption.text: 输入高于约 4.4 V：输出稳在 3.3 V。再往下，输出只比输入低一个压差，跟着一起掉；掉到欠压线，芯片复位。

i18n.en: Above about 4.4 V in: the output holds at 3.3 V. Below that, the output sits one dropout under the input and falls with it; at the brown-out line the chip resets.

en.title: Regulator dropout: when the battery runs down
en.summary: The ESP32 runs without USB, only from an LM1117-3.3 regulator. Turn the input down like a lithium cell running flat: when does the 3.3 V give way, and when does the chip reset?
en.description: Bench supply → LM1117-3.3 (10 µF on the input and the output) → the ESP32's 3V3 pin, with the ESP32's USB unplugged; a GPIO set HIGH drives a red LED through 330 Ω to show the chip is running. A linear regulator can only step down, and its input must sit at least one dropout above the output (about 1.1 V here); all the extra voltage turns into heat.

cards.title: Run a battery down, slowly
text: This time the ESP32 has **no USB**: click it and untick **USB power** in Properties on the right. It only gets what you give it.

The **bench supply** (`5 V`) + goes to the IN pin of an **LM1117-3.3** (printed face towards you, the pins are GND, OUT, IN); the regulator's OUT goes to the ESP32's **3V3** pin, and all the GNDs join.
Set any GPIO to **output HIGH** and drive a **red LED** through **`330 Ω`** to GND. While the LED is lit, the chip is running.
Now turn the bench supply down from `5 V`, **a little at a time**, like a lithium cell running flat. Where does the LED go out? The input still has more than 3 V — why is that not enough?

cards.title: A regulator is a tap that turns itself
text: - A linear regulator is like a **tap that turns itself**, sitting between input and output. It eats whatever extra voltage the input has, so the output stays at 3.3 V.

- But even wide open, the tap eats a slice of voltage of its own: the **dropout**. Once the input falls further, the output has to fall with it. In this simulator the LM1117's dropout is 1.1 V plus 0.2 Ω:
- With numbers: input 3.6 V and 0.05 A, $V_{OUT} = 3.6 - 1.1 - 0.2 × 0.05 = 2.49$ V. That is below the ESP32's brown-out line: the chip resets, every pin lets go, and the LED goes dark.
![](fig:dropout)
- The other way round, with a high input the output is still 3.3 V, but the extra voltage times the current all turns into **heat** in the regulator.

cards.title: Add the capacitors, measure again
text: - Two **`10 µF`** capacitors: one from IN to GND and one from OUT to GND, both right next to the regulator. A real LM1117 without its output capacitor can oscillate.
- Set the supply back to **`5 V`** and press **Check my circuit**. The check sets the supply to 5 V, 4.0 V, 3.7 V, 3.4 V and 9 V in turn and looks at the output and the LED.
- Once it passes, set the supply as each question says and read the multimeter and ammeter. Predict first: is 4.0 V on the wide-open stretch of the tap?
- The 9 V questions work out the regulator's heat: the voltage across it times the current through it.

cards.title: Take away
text: - **A linear regulator only steps down**, and its input must stay at least one dropout above the output (about 1.1 V for the LM1117). Below that, the output follows the input down.
- All the extra voltage becomes heat: $P = (V_{IN} - V_{OUT}) × I$. From 12 V down to 3.3 V most of the energy is burned in the regulator; that is a job for a switching supply.

- A real-world catch: **one lithium cell (3.0–4.2 V) + AMS1117-3.3** is the classic mistake. Once the cell drops to about 4 V the 3.3 V gives way, and the ESP32 reboots as soon as Wi-Fi transmits. Choose a **low-dropout regulator** with only 0.1–0.25 V (ME6211, HT7333).
- When an outside supply feeds the 3V3 pin, **don't plug in USB as well**: the two supplies fight.

compare: - **5 V**: regulating, OUT = **3.30 V**; load ≈ **56 mA**, the supply gives 61 mA (the extra 5 mA is the regulator's own quiescent current). Dissipation P = (5.0 − 3.3) × 0.056 ≈ **0.12 W**, efficiency 66 %.
- **4.0 V**: in **dropout**, OUT = 4.0 − 1.1 − 0.2 Ω × I ≈ **2.89 V**; the ESP32 still runs and the LED dims.
- **3.7 V** (a Li-ion cell's nominal voltage): OUT ≈ **2.59 V**, just above the brown-out threshold. A GPIO "HIGH" is now only about 2.6 V.
- **3.4 V** (an almost empty Li-ion cell): OUT ≈ **2.29 V**, the ESP32 **browns out**, every pin goes high-impedance and the LED goes off.
- **9 V**: still 3.30 V, but the regulator turns (9 − 3.3) × 0.056 ≈ **0.36 W** into heat; efficiency only 37 %.
- With Wi-Fi on, an ESP32 peaks at 300–500 mA: from 5 V that is 0.5–0.85 W, already very hot for a small SOT-223.

measurements.ask: Supply at 4.0 V: the regulator's OUT to GND
measurements.explain: Dropout: OUT ≈ 4.0 − 1.1 − 0.2 Ω × I ≈ 2.89 V, no longer 3.3 V.

measurements.ask: Supply at 9 V: the drop across the regulator V_IN − V_OUT (red lead on IN, black on OUT)
measurements.explain: 9 − 3.3 ≈ 5.7 V: the regulator eats more than half of the input voltage.

measurements.ask: Supply at 9 V: the regulator's output current (put the ammeter in the wire from OUT to the ESP32's 3V3)
measurements.explain: About 50 mA for the ESP32 chip plus about 4 mA for the LED. The input current is almost the same: the current passes, the voltage is eaten.

measurements.ask: Heat in the regulator at 9 V: P = (V_IN − V_OUT) × I (from your readings)
measurements.explain: A linear regulator turns all the extra voltage into heat: (9 − 3.3) V × 56 mA ≈ 0.32 W, an efficiency of only 3.3/9 ≈ 37%.

choices: goes out: the output is below the brown-out line, the ESP32 resets and every pin lets go
stays lit, just a little dimmer
burns out: a lower voltage means a bigger current
measurements.explain: 3.4 − 1.1 − 0.2 × 0.05 ≈ 2.3 V, below the ESP32's brown-out line (2.5 V in the simulator). After the reset the pins are high-impedance and the LED gets no current.

hints: With the LM1117's printed face towards you, the pins are GND, OUT, IN. The supply goes to IN (the right-hand pin).
10 µF from IN to GND and 10 µF from OUT to GND; OUT goes to the ESP32's 3V3 pin.
Click the ESP32 and untick USB power in Properties — otherwise it runs from USB and the regulator shows nothing.
tests: 4.0 V in: dropout, ESP32 still running
3.7 V in (Li-ion): a GPIO HIGH drops too
3.4 V in: ESP32 browns out, LED off
9 V in: still regulating, but the regulator heats up

tests.name: 输入 4.0 V：压差区，ESP32 还在运行
输入 3.7 V（锂电池）：GPIO 的高电平也跟着降低
输入 3.4 V：ESP32 欠压复位，LED 灭
输入 9 V：仍然稳压，但稳压器发热

compare: - **3.7 V**（锂电池的标称电压）：OUT ≈ **2.59 V**，ESP32 刚刚高于欠压阈值。GPIO 的“高电平”也只有 2.6 V 左右。
- **3.4 V**（锂电池快没电）：OUT ≈ **2.29 V**，ESP32 **欠压复位**，所有引脚变高阻，LED 灭。
- ESP32 开 Wi-Fi 时峰值电流 300–500 mA：从 5 V 降压要发热 0.5–0.85 W，SOT-223 小封装已经很烫。

measurements.ask: 电源调到 4.0 V：稳压器 OUT 对 GND 的电压
measurements.explain: 进入压差区：OUT ≈ 4.0 − 1.1 − 0.2 Ω × I ≈ 2.89 V，已经不是 3.3 V。

measurements.ask: 电源调到 9 V：稳压器上的压降 V_IN − V_OUT（红表笔 IN，黑表笔 OUT）
measurements.explain: 9 − 3.3 ≈ 5.7 V：输入里一大半的电压被稳压器吃掉了。

measurements.ask: 电源调到 9 V：稳压器的输出电流（把电流表串进 OUT 到 ESP32 3V3 的连线里读）
measurements.explain: ESP32 芯片约 50 mA，加上 LED 约 4 mA。输入电流几乎一样，所以稳压器是“电流照样过，电压被吃掉”。

measurements.ask: 9 V 时稳压器的发热 P = (V_IN − V_OUT) × I（用你的读数算）
measurements.explain: 线性稳压器把多余的电压全变成热：(9 − 3.3) V × 56 mA ≈ 0.32 W，效率只有 3.3/9 ≈ 37%。

choices: 灭：输出低于欠压线，ESP32 复位，所有引脚松开
烧掉：电压太低，电流变大
measurements.explain: 3.4 − 1.1 − 0.2 × 0.05 ≈ 2.3 V，低于 ESP32 的欠压线（仿真取 2.5 V）。芯片复位后引脚变成高阻，LED 没有电流。

hints: LM1117 正面朝你，三只脚依次是 GND、OUT、IN。电源接 IN（右边那只脚）。
IN 到 GND 一个 10 µF，OUT 到 GND 一个 10 µF；OUT 接 ESP32 的 3V3 脚。
单击 ESP32，在「属性」里取消勾选「USB 供电」——否则它从 USB 取电，就看不出稳压器的作用。
